title: Signal · Thursday 29 October
overview: Bern sets out its path to binding AI rules, Swiss banks stay loyal to core systems they rate poorly on AI, and Canada's big banks shut out personal AI agents.
status_line: Complete edition: the fixed sources opened on this run, so it adds the Swiss stories this morning's lighter briefing missed.

top.headline: Federal Council plans binding AI rules, with consultation due in spring 2027
top.summary: On 28 October the Federal Council took note of progress in applying the Council of Europe AI Convention, which it decided to ratify in February 2025. OFCOM published a report on sector-specific AI measures and a guide with model texts on 10 topics for voluntary codes of conduct. The Federal Office of Justice is drafting binding rules on transparency, data protection, non-discrimination, supervision and risk assessment, with consultation due to start in spring 2027.
top.background: Switzerland chose to ratify the convention and adapt sector laws rather than adopt a horizontal law like the EU AI Act. OFCOM's report says sectors tied to data processing and regulated markets face particular challenges.
top.why: Banks now have a dated horizon for binding Swiss AI duties alongside FINMA's supervisory expectations, so AI governance built today should map to those five themes.
top.watch_next: The Federal Office of Justice draft in spring 2027, and whether banking associations take up OFCOM's code of conduct guide.

top.headline: Swiss banks stay loyal to Finnova and Avaloq but rate their AI poorly
top.summary: The Institute of Financial Services Zug (IFZ) at Lucerne University of Applied Sciences surveyed IT executives at Swiss and Liechtenstein banks; 63 of 123 responded. 65 percent expect to keep their core banking vendor for ten years, up from 32 percent in 2023, and 68 percent innovate mainly in systems around the core. 41 percent rank AI integration among the top three future requirements, yet core systems score about two out of five on it.
top.background: Among respondents, Finnova runs 63 percent of cores and Avaloq 22 percent, according to Inside IT. The authors call the market a duopoly in which new vendors have not broken in.
top.why: AI in Swiss banking will arrive mostly in the layer around the core, which favours integration, data access and orchestration work over replacement projects.
top.watch_next: How Finnova and Avaloq answer with AI roadmaps, and whether the 62 percent who find integration demanding push for better interfaces.

top.headline: Canada's big banks block personal AI agents from online banking
top.summary: RBC, BMO, TD and CIBC say they do not let third-party personal AI agents access online banking or act for clients, according to The Canadian Press. Scotiabank will restrict such agents while it monitors concerns; National Bank is not blocking them and is watching how they develop. RBC chief executive Dave McKay wrote that nothing is more important than the security of client information.
top.background: Consumer agents from the AI labs can now log in to websites and complete tasks for users, which puts credentials and transactions in the hands of software the bank does not control.
top.why: This is an early sector-wide stance on agents acting for clients. Swiss and European banks face the same choice between blocking agents and offering approved channels.
top.watch_next: Whether banks follow with sanctioned agent access, such as delegated logins or APIs with limited permissions.

items.headline: Schwab switches on Claude for advisers and covers smaller RIAs' seat costs
items.summary: Claude for Financial Advisors went live on Schwab's platform for registered investment advisers on 28 October, at Schwab Impact in Boston, according to WealthManagement.com. Firms signing up for the enterprise plan by 30 November get a $4,800 credit, equal to the 20-seat, 12-month minimum. Schwab also added Wealth.com's estate tool Ester and invested in Nevis, an AI back-office platform.
items.why: A custodian subsidising AI seats for small advisers shows the platform contest in wealth moving to who hosts the AI layer.

items.headline: BNY adds XRP and RLUSD custody and explores tokenised receivables with Ripple
items.summary: BNY's Digital Asset Custody platform now supports XRP and Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin for eligible institutional clients, according to Fintech News Switzerland. With working capital platform C2FO, the two will explore supply chain finance using tokenised trade receivables on the XRP Ledger. Clients may later mint and redeem RLUSD through BNY, subject to approvals.
items.why: A global custodian adding stablecoin custody raises the bar for Swiss custodians courting digital asset clients.

items.headline: Wealthsimple raises up to CA$425 million at a CA$13.8 billion valuation
items.summary: GIC leads the round, which includes a CA$300 million primary offering and up to CA$125 million in secondary sales, according to Fintech News Switzerland. Assets under administration reached CA$169.2 billion at 30 September, and in the second quarter new chequing accounts outpaced new investment accounts for the first time.
items.why: A digital wealth platform moving into everyday banking shows the route neobrokers take to win primary relationships from incumbent banks.

items.headline: Vontobel reaches a record CHF 255.1 billion in assets despite institutional outflows
items.summary: Assets under management rose CHF 14.4 billion in nine months, according to finews.ch. Reported net new money was CHF 1.9 billion, or CHF 8.4 billion adjusted, with Private Clients bringing in CHF 3.8 billion. Institutional Clients lost CHF 2.0 billion, after CHF 5.1 billion left Quality Growth strategies and CHF 1.6 billion followed Raiffeisen's move of the Futura funds mandate.
items.why: Private client inflows are carrying Swiss wealth managers while asset management mandates move, which keeps pressure on fees and product ranges.

items.headline: Ermotti calls the Council of States' capital decision for UBS very concerning
items.summary: On the results call on 28 October, UBS chief executive Sergio Ermotti said the latest proposal would excessively tighten capital requirements already among the strictest in the world, according to finews.com. He said requiring foreign subsidiaries to be backed 50 percent by equity would have been more balanced, and declined to say what UBS might do if the rules stay strict.
items.why: The next parliamentary round keeps uncertainty over UBS's capital, buybacks and domicile alive for its clients and competitors.

items.headline: Hong Kong has overtaken Switzerland as the top cross-border wealth hub
items.summary: Citing a BCG study, finews.ch reports that Hong Kong passed Switzerland in 2025, with nearly 60 percent of its assets from mainland Chinese investors. Switzerland still books about $2.9 trillion of cross-border assets, and about 46 percent of assets managed there belong to clients abroad. August Benz of the Swiss Bankers Association sees growth in the Middle East and parts of Asia and Latin America.
items.why: Swiss private banks defending international clients will need sharper service and booking-centre offers as Asian hubs gain scale.

items.headline: Deutsche Bank posts a third straight record quarter with 47 billion euros of inflows
items.summary: Profit after tax was 1.9 billion euros and pre-tax profit rose 8 percent to 2.6 billion euros on revenue of 8.3 billion euros, the bank said. Private Bank and Asset Management took in record net inflows of 47 billion euros, lifting assets under management to 2.0 trillion euros. The cost/income ratio fell to 62.4 percent.
items.why: Strong private bank and asset management inflows sharpen Deutsche Bank's competition with Swiss wealth managers for European clients.

items.headline: BNP Paribas lifts profit 13.5 percent as European banks mostly beat forecasts
items.summary: BNP Paribas said net income attributable to the group rose to 3,456 million euros on revenue up 9.5 percent, and it will launch a 1.3 billion euro buyback in November. Santander's underlying profit rose 19 percent but Brazil weighed on its shares, while Standard Chartered beat estimates and raised its targets, according to Reuters.
items.why: Europe's largest banks are pairing revenue growth with cost discipline, the benchmark mid-sized Swiss banks are measured against.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO plan targets up to $2 trillion, with founders keeping control
items.summary: Anthropic plans to list in New York at a valuation of up to $2 trillion, according to SRF. Revenue exceeded $16 billion in the first half of the year. Five share classes give the seven founders 50.1 percent of the votes, and UBS is in the syndicate but not among the lead banks. The date, share count and price are not yet set.
items.why: Banks standardising on Claude will get public-company disclosure on Anthropic's finances and governance, which helps their vendor risk reviews.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, first for cyber defenders
items.summary: Google's new frontier model reaches organisations in its Fairwind Program later this week, so they can fix security flaws before a broad release, according to SiliconANGLE. Google says internal tests show it is more than twice as good at generating secure code as its predecessor, and that it halves unsupported claims compared with Gemini 4 Argon, released two weeks earlier.
items.why: Staged access by risk is becoming the norm for frontier releases, which matters to bank CISOs planning how fast such models can be approved internally.

items.headline: Microsoft previews a managed agent harness in Foundry, free until 1 December
items.summary: The Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service runs the agent loop and sandbox while developers supply skills, tools and MCP connections; agents can run code and delegate to subagents, Microsoft said. Runtime is free until 1 December, then sandbox compute costs $0.0994 per vCPU-hour and $0.0118 per GiB-hour, with model inference billed separately.
items.why: Banks on Azure get a managed way to run agents with skills and tools inside their own tenant, which eases the hosting question in architecture reviews.
items.for_your_skills: Architecture & TOM can offer a managed Azure option for hosting agents with skills and MCP tools, with published sandbox prices.

items.headline: Slack opens code channels to agents, with Anthropic among launch partners
items.summary: The Slack Code API, generally available on all Slack plans, lets agents open a code channel, add people and files, post progress, show diffs and previews, and archive the channel when done, Slack said. Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub and Vercel are launch partners, and merging approved GitHub pull requests from the channel is coming.
items.why: Agent work in channels that inherit existing permissions leaves a visible trail, which bank compliance teams will want before approving coding agents.

items.headline: Lausanne's Giotto launches two reasoning models built for Swiss and European hosting
items.summary: Giotto Solo runs on a single GPU and Giotto Alto on eight Nvidia B300 GPUs; both can run on a shared European cloud, a dedicated cloud in Switzerland or Europe, or on premises, according to ICTjournal. The company says its services meet GDPR requirements and do not depend on US cloud infrastructure. The article gives no benchmark results.
items.why: Swiss banks wary of US hyperscalers get another sovereign option to test, though its performance against the leading labs is unproven.

say_it_today: Most Swiss banks expect to keep their core banking vendor for a decade while rating its AI at two out of five, so AI will arrive in the layer around the core, where data access and integration decide what is possible.
